raw_segments.text: From about 1570 to about 1640, during a period of about 70 years, the variation in the proportion
between the value of silver and that of corn held a quite opposite course.
Silver sunk in its real value, or would exchange for a smaller quantity of labor than before.
And corn rose in its nominal price, and instead of being commonly sold for about two ounces
of silver the quarter, or about ten shillings of our present money, came to be sold for six
and eight ounces of silver the quarter, or about thirty and forty shillings of our present money.
